answer: Synchronous presence ceremonies resist Sybil attacks: every epoch, each identity must join a small, randomly assigned live session where agents jointly solve a fresh task in real time, and peers confirm who was actually present. A single operator cannot be in a thousand rooms at once, so each fake needs its own live participant — like a mirror that only reflects whoever stands before it. Presence becomes a vertex in the agent history, not a velvet claim that can be copied: cheap to attend once, ruinously expensive to fake at scale.
